implications: The judges and synthesis step should not use any claim about Oct–Dec seasonal demand, the 2026 unemployment rate, consumer spending, the winter 2026–27 forecast, La Niña/El Niño status or competitor counts unless another dossier gives it a source URL that was actually opened. This sweep verified none of these.

Other dossiers may say demand for a service is 'seasonal' or 'peaks in the fall', for example snow-removal sign-ups, holiday lights, leaf cleanup or moving. Treat those as unverified unless they cite a primary source.

Snow-removal models depend on the weather. Until someone verifies an official ECCC seasonal forecast and the NOAA/ECCC ENSO status, the plan should assume snowfall in winter 2026–27 is unknown. Any snow-contract revenue projection should include a low-snow scenario and a refund/cancellation policy. This is a planning safeguard, not a forecast.
Metro Vancouver needs its own check before any snow-based model is recommended there. This sweep did not verify its snowfall norms.

To fix this: re-run this sweep after raising CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION and allowlisting at least www150.statcan.gc.ca, www.canada.ca, weather.gc.ca, www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov, www.theweathernetwork.com, www.farmersalmanac.com, www.almanac.com, homestars.com, www.kijiji.ca and www.reddit.com.
